extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing news stories about illness, surgical operations, deaths, and related special-occasion event reporting; emphasizes newsworthiness, human-interest development, dignity of treatment, and obituary construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of illness and death stories
rubrics_metrics.description: In this class of news stories are included those concerning the illness or death of persons known in the community or in the world at large, as well as those dealing with illness, surgical operations, and deaths that are sufficiently unusual to be matters of general interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this category for reports about notable individuals, unusual or broadly interesting illnesses/deaths, surgical operations, and cases where the personal element makes the story newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary informative character with personal element
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories of this kind are primarily informative in character, but the importance of the personal element permits effective human interest development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an informative core—facts, dates, causes—while incorporating personal details, anecdotes, or human-interest touches that clarify the human impact or significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of pathetic (pathos) phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Pathetic phases of illness or death sometimes give value to news that otherwise would be of slight interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, include poignant or moving details (without sensationalism) to increase reader interest and illustrate the emotional consequences of illness or death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The seriousness of the subject demands dignity of treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a respectful tone; avoid flippancy, crude humor, or sensational language when reporting illness, dying, or death. Prioritize sensitivity to family, cultural practices, and the gravity of the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of an obituary
rubrics_metrics.description: In writing an obituary the purpose should be not only to give biographical facts but to bring out the significance of a personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well written obituary is a constructive interpretation of the meaning of a person's life and work: include essential biographical facts plus analysis, achievements, influence, and the larger significance of the deceased's life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event reporting: descriptive, scenic detail
rubrics_metrics.description: For exhibitions, entertainments and special occasions, vivid description of costumes, settings and atmosphere is important (examples in text: detailed costumes, garden booths, Arcady grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensory detail to recreate the scene (costumes, colors, lighting, setting). Names of costume types, visual motifs, and specific props/arrangements add color and credibility. Balance description with factual reporting so the picture enhances rather than obscures the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify organizers, participants and assistants by name
rubrics_metrics.description: List the persons in charge and those serving (examples: Miss Felice Lyne and her assistants, lists of venders and servers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name organizers, performers, booth attendants and helpers where relevant; include their roles or titles to document responsibility and give human faces to the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name prominent attendees and officials with titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the presence and titles of notable attendees (examples: Archbishop Farley, Mayor McClellan, diplomatic representatives and consul-generals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dignitaries or public officials attend, report their names, offices/titles, and any visible emblems. Their presence signals the event's importance and provides authoritative context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe ceremonies, processions, music and speeches
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the order of ceremonies (processions of altar boys, clergy, chanting of Te Deum), music selections, sermon topics and the languages used (English, Magyar), and include notable quotations or paraphrases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the sequence of ceremonial actions, significant musical pieces, speakers' texts or themes, and notable language choices; include short quoted phrases or paraphrase to convey tone and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include factual breakdowns and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report concrete counts and distributions when relevant (examples: number of degrees conferred and breakdown by school; class statistics such as average height, weight, age; lists of honorary degree recipients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numerical specifics (totals, breakdowns by category) to give readers quantitative sense of scale and achievement; attribute or explain figures when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgical/medical-operation reporting: method, immediate action and outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Report surgical operations with particulars of the procedure and the immediate outcome (examples: opening the abdomen and massaging the heart for seven minutes, resulting in revival; operation to relieve skull pressure and change behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the medical intervention clearly (what was done, by whom, timing), the patient's condition before and after, and any expert commentary on significance or implications. Avoid gratuitous clinical detail; respect privacy and medical ethics while explaining why the case is newsworthy (e.g., novel technique, dramatic rescue, broader social implications).
